chunks: From him, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskhan, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.أَيُّوبَ بْنِ نُوحٍ: Ayoub ibn Nuh, a prominent Shia narrator
key_terms.صَفْوَانَ: Safwan ibn Yahya, a key narrator
key_terms.مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ الْحَلَبِيِّ: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi, a narrator

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'Like it' mean in this hadith chain?
ai.summary: This concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) appears in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter determining the permissible number of wives, serving as a corroborative report identical to the preceding hadith. Its brevity underscores the consensus among early Shia jurists regarding the specific legal ruling on polygyny, reflecting the methodological precision of the *Tahdhib* in preserving authoritative chains without redundant elaboration.
